title: Electric trimmer
prompt: an electric hedge trimmer with a sprig held at its teeth on a table with three buttons: “Start” moves the blades back and forth; “Feed” brings the sprig into the teeth and clips it; “Slow” reduces the cutting speed; see-through reveals the motor, crank linkage and opposed serrated blades
blurb: A teaching adaptation of a hedge trimmer shows how a motor and opposed eccentric cams slide two serrated blades past one another to clip a sprig.
teachingAdaptations: Enlarged internal clearances and fewer teeth make the crank-cam drive legible.
Start toggles power; Slow toggles an uncalibrated slower teaching view.
Feed slides a specimen in a separate bench holder and replaces it on the next run after a cut.
The holder and specimen replacement are teaching controls, not self-feeding or self-repair hardware.
mechanism: Corded motor and reduction gear drive two 180-degree opposed eccentric cams engaging transverse blade-yoke slots; a guide bar and shoulder bolts constrain the serrated blades to longitudinal sliding.

sourceEvidence.reproduction: Educational adaptation, not an exact illustration or verified edition union.

research.title: Black and Decker double cam drive for two reciprocating cutting blades
research.supports: Two circular cams in transverse follower slots drive counter-reciprocating blade yokes.
